title: Introduce confidence-normalized regression gate and replay rate-limiter
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: CI flakiness from prompt-set regressions is often correlated with low-confidence outputs and concentrated replay bursts. This PR implements a confidence-normalized regression gate and a replay rate-limiter (replay throttle) to reduce noisy failures and protect downstream infra during automated backfills. The two pieces work together: the gate reduces false-positive failures by normalizing metric thresholds against the model's confidence distribution; the replay limiter spaces out automated replays and applies progressive quarantine for consistently flaky prompts.

What this changes: introduced a new gate type `confidence_normalized_threshold` that computes an adjusted pass threshold per-cohort using a running calibration of model confidence (softmax entropy + median logit gap). The gate can be enabled per-prompt-set and configured with a normalization window and minimum-sample floor to avoid over-calibration on small cohorts. Added a replay controller `replay_rate_limiter` used by the checkpoint replay system and the CI smoke-runner to rate-limit replays by cohort, with backoff and quarantine semantics for repeatedly failing examples.

Design summary (high-level):
- Confidence normalization: compute cohort-level confidence_factor = clamp(1.0 + alpha * (baseline_entropy - observed_entropy), 0.6, 1.4). Adjust raw metric threshold = base_threshold * confidence_factor. This reduces spurious failures when models are broadly uncertain and tightens thresholds when model confidence increases.
- Replay rate-limiter: token-bucket per-cohort with configurable burst and sustained rates, plus an exponential backoff for examples that fail 2+ consecutive replays. After N_quarantine_failures an example is marked as `quarantined` and excluded from automated replay until a manual triage or a TTL expires.
- Flaky suppression: aggregated flaky score stored alongside evaluation metadata to drive downstream triage dashboards and reduce pager noise.

Config example (single string YAML blob included in one field below in the changed files):
```
evaluation_gates:
  - name: confidence_normalized_threshold
    type: confidence_normalized
    params:
      base_threshold: 0.88
      alpha: 0.25
      normalization_window_days: 14
      min_samples: 50
      clamp_min: 0.6
      clamp_max: 1.4
replay_controller:
  type: replay_rate_limiter
  params:
    burst_per_minute: 10
    sustain_per_minute: 2
    backoff_multiplier: 2.0
    quarantine_after: 3
    quarantine_ttl_hours: 48
```

Files changed (high-level): added gate implementation, replay controller, unit tests, integration test harness, docs and a small console-dashboard hook for flaky counts. See `files_changed` for specifics.

Testing and validation: local unit tests (coverage added around gate math and throttle behavior), integration run against a real nightly model profile (ran with `smoke-run --profile nightly-2024-11-01 --dry-run=false`) and a staged CI on `staging-evals` that exercised backoff/quarantine paths. Observed reduction in false-positive failures on a 2-week retrospective run: failing PRs attributable to low-confidence prompts down 42% and total replay volume during backfills reduced by ~63% with default limits.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged gate + controller. Default off for existing prompt-sets; opt-in via prompt-set metadata. Gradual enablement for high-volume cohorts first, then all cohorts after 2 weeks of monitoring. Dashboard shows quarantined counts and replay volume.

Related: references ENG-1984 (rollout stability), ENG-2009 (replay orchestration improvements) and SUP-1132 (support ticket highlighting noisy regressions).

- [x] Integration smoke runs against nightly profile
- [x] Dashboard metric for quarantined prompt count
- [x] Docs: short-runbook and config examples
- [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout notes

patch_snippets:
--- a/eval-harness/gates/confidence_normalized_gate.py
+++ b/eval-harness/gates/confidence_normalized_gate.py
@@ def adjusted_threshold(base_threshold, alpha, observed_entropy, baseline_entropy):
-    return base_threshold
+    factor = 1.0 + alpha * (baseline_entropy - observed_entropy)
+    factor = max(min(factor, 1.4), 0.6)
+    return base_threshold * factor
--- a/eval-harness/replay/replay_rate_limiter.py
+++ b/eval-harness/replay/replay_rate_limiter.py
@@ class ReplayRateLimiter:
-    def allow(self, cohort):
-        # naive always-allow for initial implementation
-        return True
+    def allow(self, cohort):
+        # token-bucket per-cohort: burst + sustained enforcement
+        self._refill_tokens(cohort)
+        if self._tokens[cohort] > 0:
+            self._tokens[cohort] -= 1
+            return True
+        return False

ci_summary: E2E backfill smoke: pass (replay exercised with rate-limiter)
discussion_highlights: Decision to normalize against cohort entropy rather than raw confidence per-example to reduce sensitivity to single-example noise.
Telemetry added for: adjusted_threshold_applied, replay_throttle_hit, example_quarantined. These appear in the console flaky widget.
Rollout will use feature-flag and two-week monitoring window; default off for existing prompt-sets to avoid surprises.
release_notes: Add confidence-normalized evaluation gate and replay rate-limiter to reduce false-positive regression failures and control replay load. Feature-flagged; opt-in per prompt-set. Adds telemetry for throttles and quarantines.
notes_for_ops: If large cohorts start hitting quarantines unexpectedly, increase min_samples or disable the gate; replay rate limits are configurable via eval-harness config and can be relaxed per-cohort. Dashboards: evals.replay.throttle.hits and evals.quarantine.count show impact.
post_merge_actions: Monitor evals.quarantine.count and evals.replay.throttle.hits for first 2 weeks
Enable gate for two low-volume cohorts as canary after merge
Schedule follow-up (ENG-2009) to autosuggest per-cohort params based on historical traffic
